data.title: What was observed
data.narration: Every decision starts from a recorded observation carrying its provider, feed, source time and payload hash. The underlying price is the last completed daily close, never a forming bar — the system cannot see a price it would not have had.

data.title: What the code decided before the model ran
data.narration: A deterministic classifier chose the direction and set the invalidation conditions. Both were fixed before any model was called, and the model has no field in which to return either.

data.title: What the model contributed
data.narration: The model returned a memo under a strict schema: direction, confidence, cited and counter-cited evidence, and a summary. A direction that disagrees with the setup is coerced to neutral and recorded as an attempt. This is its entire authority.

data.title: What was authorized
data.narration: Deterministic risk sized the position and an immutable intent was recorded. The client order id is derived from the intent hash, so a duplicate submit collides at the broker instead of opening a second position.

data.title: What Alpaca actually did
data.narration: One Paper round trip, reconciled to flat. Acknowledgement was recorded as SUBMITTED; the fills were written only from a reconciled broker record. The round trip lost money, which is on screen because a demo that shows only the winning trade is a brochure.

data.title: What refusal looks like
data.narration: The setup did not qualify, so the model was never called. There is no memo to reject — the question never reached it. This costs one classifier and no tokens, and is recorded with the same evidence hashes as a trade.

data.what_this_is: A read-only view of decisions this system already made. It has no controls: it cannot start a run, approve an intent, or reach a broker.
disclosures: Alpaca **Paper** only. No live endpoint exists in this build.
Option quotes come from the **indicative** feed. The account has no OPRA agreement, so quotes are not trading-quality.
**No alpha is claimed.** A `NO_TRADE` refusal and a deterministic baseline beating the model are both valid results.
Nothing here is investment advice.

data.write_guards_note: They run before every order rather than at startup, because the interesting failures develop between the two. Risk-reducing closes are exempt from guards 3, 4 and 5: those exist to stop new risk, and applying them to an exit would trap exposure at the moment it most needs reducing.

halt_states.explanation: New risk permitted. Closes and cancels also permitted.
New or increased risk blocked. Cancels and risk-reducing closes stay permitted, because blocking a close during a loss would trap exposure.
All writes blocked, including closes. Reserved for adapter, credential or endpoint integrity incidents, and it raises an incident precisely because it can temporarily prevent risk reduction.

why.text: A deterministic classifier (deterministic_trend_retest_v0) identified a bullish trend continuation retest setup, citing 2 signals.
It set 2 invalidation conditions: close below 759.53 invalidates the retest; loss of directional structure on the decision timeframe. The model never received these and has no schema field for them.
The model returned bullish at confidence 0.7. Its entire contribution is this memo; a direction disagreeing with the setup is coerced to neutral and recorded as an attempt.
Risk arithmetic approved the structure at a maximum loss of 362 against a budget of 750.
No intent was created. The decision resolved to OPTIONS_POSITION, so nothing was ever prepared for the broker.

signals.summary: At-the-money implied volatility is 0.0908, at or below the 0.22 calm threshold, so the option market is not pricing stress that would contradict continuation.
EMA20 is 0.0130 from EMA50 in the bullish direction, price closed at 771.1 on the bullish side of EMA20, and price retested it within the last 5 completed sessions.
